text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear claim against driverless cars from the first sentence","quality":"focused position","description":"The essay states a definite stance immediately and keeps that position consistent throughout."},{"evidence":"law, hacking, sensors, weather, liability","quality":"relevant support","description":"It develops its argument with multiple points tied to the article's concerns rather than drifting off topic."},{"evidence":"three body paragraphs with topic sentences","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is arranged into distinct sections that make its argument easier to follow."},{"evidence":"\"If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault the driver or the manufacturer?\"","quality":"use of textual evidence","description":"It quotes the source article directly to back up a claim about liability and legal uncertainty."},{"evidence":"concluding restatement of danger and unreliability","quality":"conclusion","description":"It ends by summarizing the main argument and reinforcing the overall judgment."},{"evidence":"mentions hacked cameras and damaged sensors","quality":"specificity","description":"It gives concrete examples of how driverless cars could fail instead of relying only on general complaints."}]}
